name: clio.css
description: CSS library for classic Mac OS interfaces: Macintosh System 6, System 7, Mac OS 8.5 Drawing Board and Mac OS 8/9 Platinum windows, menus, buttons, scroll bars and dialogs, with every value traced to measured pixels.

evidenceStatuses.measured: read from real pixels of the era
evidenceStatuses.inferred: reasoned from documentation or behaviour, not measured
evidenceStatuses.adapted: a deliberate departure for the web (touch, focus, contrast)
evidenceStatuses.third-party: art or font from a named, licensed project

components.name: Window
components.summary: A document window: frame, title bar with close and zoom boxes (plus the WindowShade box in Platinum), an optional details bar and a scrolling pane. System 7 adds colour to the frame and title bar.
components.accessibility: Give each box an aria-label (Close, Zoom, Collapse). The title is a real heading; pick the level that fits your page (h1 for a full-screen app window). Buttons keep a visible focus ring. On touch screens each box gets a 45px hit area while its art stays 11px.

components.name: Menu bar and menus
components.summary: The menu bar across the top of the screen and its pull-down menus: items, keyboard shortcuts, check marks, separators, disabled items and submenus.
components.accessibility: Use role=menubar, role=menu and role=menuitem with aria-haspopup and aria-expanded on titles. A menu opens while its title has aria-expanded=true, while its <li> has the class open, or while focus is inside it, so it works from the keyboard without script. Arrow-key movement between items is up to your script.
